title: DatePicker
wrapsNative: DatePicker(_:selection:in:displayedComponents: .date) with the default .compact style, inside MonarchFormField; a Menu of preset dates beside it
summary: The standard SwiftUI date picker with displayedComponents: .date, shown in a MonarchFormField row and tinted with the accent by the theme. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For one calendar date in a form: due dates, start dates, birthdays, renewal and expiry dates. Add a Menu of presets (Today, Tomorrow, In a week) beside it when people often pick the same dates.
whenNotToUse: For a date and a time, use displayedComponents: [.date, .hourAndMinute]. For a range of dates, use two pickers, the second limited by the first. For browsing a month with events, use MonarchMiniMonth.
api: DatePicker(_ title: String, selection: Binding<Date>, in range: PartialRangeFrom<Date>, displayedComponents: DatePickerComponents)

states.name: set
states.description: The compact button shows the date in the locale's format; tapping it opens the system calendar.

states.name: limited
states.description: Dates outside the `in:` range are dimmed and cannot be chosen.

states.name: optional
states.description: The app keeps a Date? and shows Set date and Clear date buttons around the picker (the system picker always has a date).

states.name: invalid
states.description: MonarchFormField shows the app's error text with its icon under the row.

appearance: The system picker: in a Monarch theme the selected day and today take the accent through the tint; the field label, helper and error come from MonarchFormField in the theme's text and danger roles.
platformNotes: The web DatePicker is a typed text field with a calendar popover, ISO string values, presets, min/max, disabled days, week numbers and Field errors. On iOS the system picker is the expected control: it formats and parses in the person's locale and calendar, so there is no typed input to validate. min and max become the `in:` range; presets are a Menu next to the picker; an optional date needs a Date? in the app. Disabled individual days, week numbers and per-day info are not offered by the system picker; for those, show MonarchMiniMonth in a sheet. The value is a Date: store it as a day (DateComponents or an ISO yyyy-MM-dd string) when it must not shift with time zones. Android uses the Material 3 DatePicker.
accessibility: System behaviour: the compact picker is a button read with its label and date; the calendar is navigable by VoiceOver with the selected day marked.
With .labelsHidden() the visible label comes from MonarchFormField, and the picker keeps its own title for VoiceOver.
Preset menu items are standard buttons.
Dynamic Type and right-to-left calendars are handled by the system.
edgeCases: A Date carries a time: compare days with Calendar.isDate(_:inSameDayAs:), and keep the start of day when saving a pure date.
A selection outside the `in:` range is clamped by the picker.
The graphical style takes the full width and about 350 points of height; use it inline only on roomy screens.
